# What we have, and what comes next

## Eleven packages, ten registered, two empty repos

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="52%"}
- 22 repositories, 19 of them public. 11 hold a Julia package, 10 of
  those are in General. `ScoringRules.jl` is not registered
- Six distribution packages, one fitting protocol, one Turing layer, one
  scoring port, one package kit, one automatic differentiation toolbox
- `GenerationTime.jl` and `ReproductionNumber.jl` were created in
  February and have never been pushed to
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
- The documentation site lists ten of the eleven. `ScoringRules.jl` is
  missing, and the deployed site trails `main` by one more
- The abstract for this talk says we have `CensoredDistributions.jl` and
  an R interface prototype. It is ten packages behind, and the prototype
  points at the old CDC `EpiAware` package rather than anything here

::: {.attribution}
The R prototype is `sbfnk/EpiAwareR`, by Sebastian Funk. Last pushed
2026-06-22, about seven weeks ago.
:::
:::
::::

## The style guide is a failing test

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
```julia
const BANNED_README_WORDS = [
    "comprehensive", "cornerstone",
    "facilitate", "foster",
    "framework", "harness",
    "landscape", "leverage",
    "novel", "pivotal",
    "practitioner", "robust",
    "streamline", "synergy",
    # ... 20 in total
]
```
:::
::: {.column width="52%"}
- Nine quality checks run in every package. Aqua, ExplicitImports,
  import centralisation, docstring format, README sections, doctests,
  formatting, JET, extension ambiguities
- `EpiAwarePackageTools.jl` writes up to 69 files into a package, most
  of them force-managed, so a package cannot drift from the standard
- Ten of the eleven are on it. The exception is the package the tooling
  was extracted from. Uniformity is the point, and an agent that has
  learned one repository has learned all of them
- The bill is 8,600 lines of Julia to hold eleven packages rigid, and a
  contributor cannot change one repository's tooling on their own

::: {.callout-note}
A guideline gets ignored. A failing test does not.
:::
:::
::::

## What we said we would build, and where it has got to

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Distribution extensions**
Six packages, all registered. Enough to build on.

**Delay and generation time estimation**
`DistributionsInference.jl` is the fit protocol. `GenerationTime.jl` has
been an empty repository since February.
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Disease dynamics**
`ComposableTuringIDModels.jl` is the Turing layer.
`ReproductionNumber.jl` is empty too.

**Forecast evaluation**
`ScoringRules.jl` runs, and is not registered.
:::
::::

- Every package also has to meet the same standard. Docstrings through
  DocStringExtensions, references through DocumenterCitations, and
  optional integrations as package extensions rather than dependencies.
  `EpiAwareADTools.jl` carries seven of them
- Sustaining it needs two things we do not have. One documentation site
  that is not behind the code, and a governance document
